name: Roman Tribunal
description: Hermetic Tribunal spanning the Italian peninsula, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, the southern Alps and northern Africa; a land of intrigue, corruption and conflict among Magi.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The Hermetic order of wizards, founded in part by ten Roman Magi, whose roots lie in the Roman Tribunal.

name: Provençal Tribunal
description: Neighboring Tribunal containing Doissetep, Windgraven and Mistridge; it feuds with the Roman Tribunal after Hermetic interference in Sicily.

name: Tribunal of the Greater Alps
description: Tribunal bordering the Roman Tribunal in the Alps, which a new Roman covenant must not infringe upon.

name: Tamgor of Quaesitor
description: Quaesitor who journeyed through the Roman Tribunal's covenants to gather information ahead of Jarane's triad, recording his findings in a journal.

name: Jarane of Quaesitor
description: Highly respected Quaesitor who plans to lead a triad of Quaesitoris into Italy to fix the Roman Tribunal's problems.

name: Arliandus of Magvillus
description: Quaesitor of Magvillus, named as perhaps the most respected member of House Quaesitor.

name: Guernicus
description: Founder of House Quaesitor, one of the three Order founders who called the Roman Tribunal home; invoked in oaths by Quaesitors.

name: Magvillus
description: Domus Magnus of House Quaesitor in the mountains of southern Italy; a scheming covenant that owns Sicily and wields great influence over the Tribunal and its Treaty.

name: House Quaesitor
description: Hermetic House of judges and investigators whose Domus Magnus is Magvillus.

name: Harco
description: Domus Magnus of House Mercere at the northwest edge of the Alps, an opulent, mercantile covenant with a Hermes Portal to Doissetep.

name: Doissetep
description: Great covenant of the Provençal Tribunal, linked to Harco by a Hermes Portal and famous for its library.

name: House Mercere
description: One of the most respected Houses of the Order, with its Domus Magnus at Harco.

name: Mercere
description: Founder of House Mercere and one of three Order founders who called the Roman Tribunal home.

name: Insatella
description: Primus of House Mercere at Harco, deeply involved in mercantile affairs and unfriendly toward Tamgor.

name: Guiseppe
description: Visiting merchant at Harco who told Tamgor the covenant was honest in its trade.

name: Hermes Portal
description: Magical portal allowing travel between covenants; Harco maintains one leading to Magvillus and to Doissetep.

name: Duresca scrolls
description: Scrolls of ages past possibly connected to the power machinations within Magvillus.

name: Sansaron
description: Isolationist covenant in magical caverns beneath a temple in the ruins of Carthage in North Africa; infiltrated by vengeful hedge wizards.

name: Ahmen
description: One of Sansaron's five custos, who met and grudgingly hosted Tamgor.

name: Narisian
description: Head of Sansaron, abrupt and unwelcoming to Tamgor.

name: Verdi
description: Domus Magnus of House Verditius, hidden in a concealed valley on Sardinia; beautiful but rife with plots to control the Tribunal.

name: House Verditius
description: Hermetic House of item-makers whose Domus Magnus is Verdi.

name: Verditius
description: Founder of House Verditius and one of the three Order founders who called the Roman Tribunal home.

name: Imanitosi
description: Primus of Verditius at Verdi, who dwells in a great mystical tower.

name: Rellantali
description: Liberal covenant on the island of Asinara with a strong ruler, suspicious of Magvillus and a longtime target of Verdi.

name: Netiriun
description: Young Magus of Rellantali who refused Tamgor entry, suspecting him of spying for Magvillus.

name: Vardian's Tomb
description: Independent covenant in the catacombs near Rome, divested from the Order and split between Jerbiton and necromancer factions.

name: Fortunatas of Jerbiton
description: One of the two heads of Vardian's Tomb.

name: Rubaton Ex Miscellanea
description: One of the two heads of Vardian's Tomb, associated with its necromancer faction.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House to which Rubaton of Vardian's Tomb belongs.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House that allied with Pope Sylvester II to found Literatus and is its most common House.

name: Postestas
description: Tremere covenant on cliffs overlooking the Adriatic, well regarded and seeking to lead a new Roman order.

name: House Tremere
description: Hermetic House with a power-hungry reputation whose members lead Postestas.

name: Garvil
description: Leader of Postestas who speaks of preserving order in the Tribunal.

name: Literatus
description: Covenant near Bologna with a vast library, founded through Pope Sylvester II and House Jerbiton, mixing mundane and magic and secretly Infernally corrupt.

name: Amberitus
description: Head of Literatus, who preaches cooperation among the Tribunal's Magi.

name: Treaty of the Roman Tribunal
description: Treaty drafted by Iernilus in 1068 limiting Magi's dealings with mundanes and sales of magic items; part of the Peripheral Code.

name: Luctatio
description: Newly founded covenant near Milan in Lombardy, led by Arasen of Tytalus.

name: Arasen
description: Hospitable Tytalus Magus who leads Luctatio.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House to which Arasen belongs.

name: Feritel
description: One of two independent covenants in Italy divested from the Tribunal.

name: House Flambeau
description: Hermetic House suited to Rellantali's missions; a Flambeau sent by Magvillus executed Juden.

name: Flambeau
description: Founder of the Order who hunted hedge wizards, destroying Vardian's Skull and slaying three hedge wizards in the catacombs near Rome.

name: Tytalus
description: Order founder who stalked and slew hedge wizards alongside Flambeau.

name: Bjornaer
description: Shapechanger founder of the Order of Hermes.

name: Diedne
description: Druid founder of the Order of Hermes.

name: Bonisagus
description: Founder who created a theory of magic; his followers at Auctus sought a new theory.

name: House Bonisagus
description: Followers of Bonisagus who joined in the covenant of Auctus.

name: House Criamon
description: Hermetic House whose followers joined at Auctus.

name: House Merinita
description: Hermetic House; a Sardinian Merinita theorizes the Mercurians fled into Faerieland.

name: Auctus
description: Covenant near Verdi where Bonisagus, Criamon and Merinita followers sought a new magic theory; destroyed by Verdi's political attacks.

name: Calabria (covenant)
description: Covenant in southern Italy weakened by a Verdi-instigated Mussulman invasion; its Magi fled to Novgorod.

name: Bellaquin
description: Provençal covenant that followed Literatus' example of joining mundane and magic.

name: Windgraven
description: Provençal covenant whose Magi accompanied Charles of Anjou to Sicily.

name: Mistridge
description: Provençal covenant, Windgraven's traditional enemy, whose Magi aided the Sicilian Vespers.

name: Iernilus
description: Stubborn, fair-minded Quaesitor who drafted the Treaty of the Roman Tribunal, finalized in 1068.

name: Juden of Verditius
description: Magus of Verdi who murdered clergy on Sardinia to restore magic and was killed under a Wizard's March.

name: Marcelo of Verdi
description: Magus of Verdi who has long tried to fathom the magic of the Roman roads.

name: Terith of Jerbiton
description: Jerbiton researcher who seeks evidence of a diabolic pact tainting Italy and theorizes the Mercurians turned to diabolism.

name: Cult of Mercury
description: Ancient Roman magical cult rooted in the Cult of Hermes, worshipping Mercury; disbanded in 412 and an inspiration for Hermetic magic.

name: Cult of Hermes
description: Greek magical cult from which the Cult of Mercury drew its ideals; its artifacts later reached Italy.

name: Hasophis
description: Legendary founder of the Cult of Mercury, said to be buried in the southern Alps.

name: Great Iron Tree
description: Legendary tree enchanted by one hundred Mercurians for a mysterious task.

name: Tarhutis
description: Ancient god worshipped by the Romans as Mercury, whose awakening may have destroyed the Cult of Mercury.

name: Mercury
description: God worshipped by the Cult of Mercury and common folk in temples throughout Italy.

name: Roman roads
description: Roads that seem to form a great magical network created with the Cult of Mercury.

name: Age of Chaos
description: Period of about 350 years after the Cult of Mercury's fall when Italian wizards lived in lawless fear and battle.

name: Hedge wizard
description: Non-Hermetic wizards, many hunted by Flambeau and Tytalus; some fled to Africa plotting revenge.

name: Vardian's Skull
description: Ancient artifact of three hedge wizards destroyed by Flambeau; its power created the Magical Aura of Vardian's Tomb.

name: Varator
description: Demon of vengeance tied to the hedge wizard refugees plotting against the Order.

name: Peris
description: Demon controlling many diabolists in northern Italy's cities, patron of the Della Torre, who took flesh as Eccelino da Romano.

name: Deriten
description: Demon who made a pact with Frederick Barbarossa and sought to claim Peris' lands.

name: Brazen Head
description: Prophetic device gained by Gerbert in Toledo, allegedly Infernal.

name: Golden dove of Constantine
description: Golden dove bearing the Holy Word that helped Constantine root out Infernal corruption; since lost.

name: Donation of Constantine
description: Document recording Constantine's gift of the Western Empire to the Papacy; those who saw it died within a year.

name: Pope Sylvester II
description: Scholar-Pope and magician who, with House Jerbiton, founded Literatus; his body vanished after his death.

name: Frederick II
description: King of Sicily and Emperor who allied with Literatus and was secretly corrupted by it; remembered as the Anti-Christ.

name: Frederick Barbarossa
description: Holy Roman Emperor and secret diabolist pawn of the demon Deriten who warred on the northern Italian cities.

name: Eccelino da Romano
description: Tyrant of Verona and Lombardy, possessed by the demon Peris until Magi drove it out in 1259.

name: Robert Guiscard
description: Norman mercenary who conquered southern Italy with magic items bought from Roman Magi.

name: Roger the Great
description: Robert Guiscard's nephew, named King of Sicily.

name: Innocent III
description: Pope whose pontificate marks the height of Papal power, possibly aided by otherworldly power.

name: Innocent IV
description: Pope who deposed and excommunicated Frederick II.

name: Gregory IX
description: Pope who excommunicated Frederick II.

name: Boniface VIII
description: Vile diabolist Pope who duped Celestine V into resigning.

name: Celestine V
description: Saintly Pope overwhelmed by intrigue and duped into resigning.

name: Pope Leo I
description: Pope who declared the Church independent and turned Attila from Rome, reputedly with demons at his command.

name: Constantine
description: Roman Emperor who recognized Christianity and, aided by a golden dove, rooted out Infernal corruption.

name: Charlemagne
description: King of the Franks and Lombards crowned Emperor of the Romans.

name: Otto III
description: German Emperor tutored by Gerbert, killed in a Roman revolt.

name: Henry III
description: German ruler who reputedly controlled popes by blackmail over diabolism.

name: Charles of Anjou
description: French count crowned King of Sicily in 1266, bringing Windgraven Magi into Italy.

name: Manfred
description: Bastard son of Frederick II, possibly demon-spawned, who took Sicily's crown before being killed.

name: Della Torre
description: Milanese family in pact with the demon Peris who organized the Lombard League.

name: Della Scala
description: Family ruling Verona.

name: Lombard League
description: Alliance of Lombard communes formed at Pontida to defeat Frederick Barbarossa, reformed against Frederick II.

name: Guelph
description: Papalist party of the northern Italian cities.

name: Ghibelline
description: Imperialist party of the northern Italian cities.

name: Podesta
description: Imperially appointed executive officers of northern communes, later kept by city councils.

name: Holy Roman Empire
description: Empire north of Italy with theoretical control over northern Italy, in conflict with the Papacy.

name: Kingdom of Sicily
description: Kingdom ruling southern Italy and Sicily, with its capital at Palermo.

name: Papal States
description: Papal domain running from Rome to Bologna.

name: Inquisition
description: Newly formed Church body against heretics, strengthened by Frederick II.

name: Saracens
description: Islamic invaders of Sicily and southern Italy; small enclaves still practice their own magic.

name: Magyars
description: Nomadic Hungarian raiders of northern Italy; small enclaves remain.

name: Lombards
description: Germanic tribe that ruled northern Italy for 200 years.

name: Visigoths
description: Germanic invaders who sacked Rome, reputedly led by a demonic monster.

name: Vandals
description: Germanic invaders who sacked Rome and conquered Sicily and Sardinia.

name: Visigoth monster
description: Huge four-armed obsidian-furred monster that led the Visigoths into Rome, banished by a young priest.

name: She-wolf of Rome
description: She-wolf that raised Romulus and Remus, perhaps a powerful faerie still living.

name: Romulus
description: Legendary founder of Rome who killed his twin Remus.

name: Remus
description: Twin of Romulus, whose shade may still haunt Rome.

name: Sirens
description: Creatures whose song on the Straits of Messina lures sailors to death.

name: Cyclopes
description: Creatures east of Sicily to whom sailors make sacrifices.

name: The Devil
description: Infernal lord seeking to corrupt Italy and destroy Christianity.

name: Infernal
description: Realm of demons whose corruption pervades Italy and the Roman Tribunal.

name: Dominion
description: Divine realm whose influence has contributed to the fading of magic in Rome.

name: Magic realm
description: Realm of magic, fading from Italy.

name: Faerie
description: Faerie realm whose Auras shrank in Italy.

name: Faerieland
description: Faerie realm where the Mercurians may have fled, where a day is a year.

name: Magical Aura
description: Mystical aura such as the one imbued in Vardian's Tomb by Vardian's Skull.

name: Vis
description: Magical resource bitterly fought over and fading in the Roman Tribunal.

name: Certamen
description: Magical duel used to compel covenants in Tribunal politics.

name: Wizard's War
description: Sanctioned magical war between Magi.

name: Wizard's March
description: Order-sanctioned death sentence, as imposed on Juden.

name: Code of Hermes
description: Hermetic law defied by Roman Magi in mundane dealings.

name: Peripheral Code
description: Body of Hermetic precedent including the Treaty of the Roman Tribunal.

name: Domus Magnus
description: A House's chief covenant.

name: Primus
description: Head of a Hermetic House.

name: Gauntlet
description: Test ending apprenticeship.

name: Custos
description: Covenant guard or servant.

name: Grog
description: Covenant soldiers or servants.

name: Covenfolk
description: Mundane covenant inhabitants.

name: Consors
description: Covenant associates used as intermediaries.

name: Magus
description: Hermetic wizard.

name: Quaesitor
description: Hermetic judge.

name: Seekers
description: Magi researching the Cult of Mercury's history.

name: Tribunal meeting
description: Gathering of a Tribunal's Magi; Roman meetings are held every seven years in Venice.

name: The Gift
description: Magical talent.

name: Invested device
description: Enchanted item; the Treaty limits sales to mundanes.

name: Rome
description: Holy city and heart of the Empire.

name: Italy
description: Peninsula forming the core of the Roman Tribunal.

name: Sicily
description: Fertile island owned by Magvillus, likely site for new covenants.

name: Sardinia
description: Island where Verdi is hidden.

name: Corsica
description: Island contested by Pisa and Genoa.

name: Asinara
description: Small island north of Sardinia where Rellantali lies.

name: Carthage
description: Ancient city whose ruins shelter Sansaron.

name: Tunis
description: North African port reputed home to pirates.

name: Cagliari
description: Sardinian port near Verdi.

name: Vieste
description: Italian port city.

name: Ostia
description: Rome's port.

name: Venice
description: City where Treaty meetings are held.

name: Milan
description: Lombard city near Luctatio.

name: Bologna
description: City near Literatus.

name: Palermo
description: Capital of the Kingdom of Sicily.

name: Lombardy
description: War-torn northern Italian region.

name: Venetia
description: Northern Italian region.

name: Calabria
description: Western southern Italian region.

name: Apulia
description: Eastern southern Italian region.

name: Po Valley
description: Beast-infested valley south of the Alps.

name: Alps
description: Mountains dividing Italy from France and the Empire.

name: Apennines
description: Mountains running the length of Italy.

name: Gulf of Taranto
description: Gulf dividing southern Italy.

name: Tyrrhenian Sea
description: Harsh western sea.

name: Adriatic Sea
description: Wild eastern sea.

name: Ionic Sea
description: Pirated southern sea.

name: Straits of Messina
description: Straits where sirens sing.

name: Mount Etna
description: Volcano to whose pit Frederick II's soul was carried.

name: Catacombs of Rome
description: Catacombs housing Vardian's Tomb.

name: Pontida
description: Monastery where the Lombard League formed.

name: Verona
description: City ruled by Della Scala and Eccelino.

name: Padua
description: City where Eccelino built eight prisons.

name: Pavia
description: Imperialist city.

name: Toledo
description: City where Gerbert learned magic and gained the Brazen Head.

name: University of Naples
description: University founded by Frederick II and staffed by former Literatus apprentices.

name: Constantinople
description: Eastern capital.

name: Novgorod
description: Distant city where Calabria's Magi fled.

name: Sicilian Vespers
description: 1282 Palermo revolt against French rule aided by Mistridge Magi.

name: Diet of Roncaglia
description: Assembly defining Imperial rights, prompting a Tribunal decree against Literatus interfering.

name: Concordat of Worms
description: 1122 agreement ending the Investiture Contest.

name: Capitulation of Neuss
description: Agreement defining Papal lands.

name: Punic Wars
description: Wars destroying Carthage, possibly with Infernal aid.

name: Albigensian heretics
description: Heretics rife in northern Italy.

name: Franciscan Order
description: Religious order supported by Innocent III.

name: Dominican Order
description: Religious order supported by Innocent III.

name: Diabolist
description: Infernal worshippers; many diabolic groups in Italy.

name: Necromancer
description: Faction at Vardian's Tomb.

name: Infernal pact
description: Bargain with a demon.
